candidates.node_relation: Direct supplier of custom-formulated sauces and salad dressings to foodservice customers and national chain restaurant accounts.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Specialty foods; foodservice sauces, dressings, frozen bakery
candidates.theme_relation: Restaurant menu innovation and chain consistency can drive demand for customized sauces, dressings and dips that are hard to switch once validated across a chain system.
candidates.why_include: Its filings explicitly describe foodservice products as custom-formulated sauces and salad dressings, and note record Foodservice sales driven by national chain restaurant account demand.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as a packaged-food or dividend company rather than as a behind-the-scenes restaurant-chain flavor and sauce supplier.

candidates.next_evidence: Review the latest 2025 annual report and Q2 2026 earnings call for Flavor Solutions sales, QSR commentary, customer concentration and input-cost pass-through.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as the benchmark against which smaller or more obscure public suppliers should be compared.

evidence.claim: Lancaster Colony's 2024 10-K stated that most Foodservice segment products are custom-formulated sauces, salad dressings, frozen breads and yeast rolls, and that Foodservice net sales rose to a record $883.3 million due partly to national chain restaurant account demand.
evidence.source_title: The Marzetti Company - 10-K - Annual Report - August 22, 2024

evidence.claim: McCormick describes itself as manufacturing and distributing herbs, spices, seasonings, condiments and flavors for retailers, food manufacturers and foodservice businesses, with Consumer and Flavor Solutions segments.

McCormick's 2025 10-K says Flavor Solutions develops seasonings for snacks and other food products and flavors for new menu items; the 2024 report noted higher sales to quick-service restaurant customers in China.
evidence.source_title: McCormick & Company, Incorporated - 10-K - Annual Report - January 23, 2025

evidence.claim: B&G Foods' 2025 10-K lists products including cooking oils, cooking sprays, spices, seasonings, hot sauces, wine vinegar, salad dressings, Mexican-style sauces, salsas, pickles and peppers, and says it sells to wholesale distributors, foodservice distributors and direct accounts among other channels.
evidence.source_title: B&G Foods, Inc. - 10-K - Annual Report - February 25, 2025

evidence.claim: TreeHouse Foods is described as a private-label packaged-food manufacturer focused on retail grocery and food-away-from-home customers, with more than 50 manufacturing facilities across the United States, Canada and Italy.

Older TreeHouse filings described food-away-from-home sales of Mexican sauces and refrigerated dressings to foodservice customers, but current direct sauces/dressings exposure requires verification because recent descriptions emphasize snacks, beverages, broths, pickles and co-manufacturing.

Ventura Foods is a private $3 billion supplier of oils, sauces, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, margarine, butter blends and seasonings to top restaurant chains and distributors, including Sysco, McDonald's, Subway, Burger King and Papa John's.
evidence.source_title: Ventura Foods Dials up Flavor to Fuel Growth at $3 Billion Supplier - Orange County Business Journal

evidence.claim: The presence of large private suppliers such as Ventura Foods implies that public screens limited to GICS restaurant, grocery or distributor labels may miss the most relevant sauce/oil/dressing chokepoint companies.
evidence.source_title: Ventura Foods Dials up Flavor to Fuel Growth at $3 Billion Supplier - Orange County Business Journal

memory_update.text: LANC is the strongest public underfollowed candidate for the sauces/dressings node because its Foodservice segment explicitly includes custom-formulated sauces and dressings for national chain restaurant customers.
MKC should remain in the reference lane as the flavor-systems benchmark, not the main underfollowed alpha candidate.
BGS is a small-cap hypothesis with direct product overlap in oils, seasonings, hot sauces and dressings, but restaurant-chain custom-supply evidence is weak and must be verified.

Ventura Foods appears highly relevant but private; later layers should map whether any public suppliers sell inputs, packaging, equipment, oils, emulsifiers, dairy fats or logistics services into Ventura, Golden State Foods, Sysco private-label programs, or comparable sauce/dressing co-manufacturers.

The key diligence variable for this node is not simply owning condiment brands; it is scaled foodservice customization, food-safety compliance, distributor/private-label access, plant capacity, customer validation and switching-cost evidence.

node: Sauces, oils, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, butter blends, and seasonings
summary: Expanded the public-company universe for the restaurant flavor-input node. The cleanest public direct exposure found is Lancaster Colony / The Marzetti Company, which reports custom-formulated sauces and salad dressings for national chain restaurant accounts. McCormick is the reference leader for scalable flavor systems and foodservice seasonings/condiments, but it is larger and more followed. B&G Foods and TreeHouse Foods are lower-attention candidates with plausible exposure through spices, oils, dressings, sauces, private-label or food-away-from-home channels, but both need verification that restaurant-chain or distributor-private-label exposure is material today. A key private-market benchmark is Ventura Foods, a large nonpublic supplier to top restaurant chains and Sysco, which supports the bottleneck hypothesis but is not itself investable via a US-listed common equity.
